built.summary: Each step is one quiet question with at most three large paper "destination cards". Each card has a mono three-letter code in a left stub, a dashed perforation, the name and a one-line detail; options with no decks yet are flat, outlined and not tappable. Tapping a card lifts it and moves its paper, perforation, code and name to the top, where they become a compact "you are here" header with a round back button. Meanwhile the old step fades back and the next cards rise in with a 40 ms stagger. Back runs the same motion in reverse, so the header returns to its slot in the list.
built.logo: The mark is a small amber boarding-pass ticket (46 x 34, rounded, with semicircle notches on both sides). It has an ink check mark for "true" and a faint dashed tear line near its right end, set beside the "Truthy" wordmark in Overpass 800 at 38px. The description line underneath, in Overpass 600 17px ink-muted: "True or false cards that teach IT, one short round at a time." Step 1 places the logo in the second sky band, so the text no longer crosses a band edge, and the three area cards sit in the thumb zone below.
built.motion:
One orchestrated shared-element transition per step change, Web Animations only, transform and opacity only.

Forward (card to header): four elements are paired by data-k (paper, perf, code, name) between the tapped card and the next step's header. Each target is moved FLIP-style from the card's rect to its own rect over 360 ms with the token ease, cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1):
- paper: translate plus scale(w, h)
- perf: translate plus scaleY
- code and name: translate plus uniform scale by font-size ratio (28 to 20, 20 to 17)

The header paper has the bigger --shadow, so the card reads as lifted the moment it leaves the list. Things only one of the two shapes has (the card's detail and chevron, the header's "All areas" / "Cloud" label) move with the paper on the same easing. Their opacity runs on linear time: the old ones fade in 80 ms, the new ones appear in the last 40%. The back button sits outside the paper and only fades in place. Everything else on the old step fades out with a scale to .96 (110 ms, ease-in). The new step's heading and cards rise from +32px with a fade (260 ms, delays 70 + i*40 ms), so the whole thing ends at about 410 ms.

Back: the same code with the roles swapped. The header's paper, perf, code and name travel back into the tapped card's slot. The current cards drop 24px and fade (110 ms). The previous step scales back from .96 with the same stagger.

Checked with frozen frames at 60, 150 and 250 ms for all four transitions (all animations paused at an exact currentTime). There is no text over text: the opaque travelling paper sits above everything it passes, and old items are gone before new ones become visible. No jump, no flash. The 150 ms frames are in design/flow/shots/browse-a-mid-{fwd1,fwd2,back3,back2}-150ms.png.

Reduced motion: no pairs, no movement. The steps fade through (old step out in 100 ms, then new step in over 160 ms) so the two headings never overlap. The sheet fades instead of sliding.

SwiftUI: put the four parts of each card under matchedGeometryEffect(id: "\(item.id).paper/perf/code/name", in: ns), with .animation(.timingCurve(0.2, 0.7, 0.2, 1, duration: 0.36)). The labels and chevrons use .transition(.opacity). The incoming list uses .transition(.move(edge: .bottom).combined(with: .opacity)) with a per-index .delay(0.07 + 0.04*i). The outgoing list uses .scale(0.96).combined(with: .opacity). Under accessibilityReduceMotion, switch to .opacity only.

Compose: SharedTransitionLayout plus AnimatedContent(targetState = step). Use Modifier.sharedBounds / sharedElement(rememberSharedContentState("${id}-paper")) for the paper, perf, code and name, with boundsTransform = tween(360, easing = CubicBezierEasing(0.2f, 0.7f, 0.2f, 1f)). Enter: slideInVertically { 32.dp } + fadeIn with a staggered delay. Exit: scaleOut(0.96f) + fadeOut(110). Use the reversed specs when going back (the targetState comparison). With reduce motion, use fadeIn/fadeOut only.
built.openQuestions:
1. Codes I made up for levels the brief didn't code: areas are CLD (Cloud), FRN (Frontend), OPS (DevOps); platforms are AWS, GCP, AZR, NXT. The AWS card's name reads "Amazon Web Services" so the name isn't a repeat of the code. The client should confirm these or supply their own.
2. The reduced-motion rule is not copied verbatim from the reference. The reference's `transition-duration: 1ms` on every element turns every inherited `visibility` change into a CSS transition, which briefly hid the header text in the next step. I used `transition: none` plus an explicit opacity fade for the sheet. This affects every screen that copies that rule, so the reference may want the same fix.
3. Steps 2 and 3 are top-aligned under the header, so the lower third of the screen is empty sky and paper. Step 1 places its cards lower, in the thumb zone. If the client wants the same card height on every step, steps 2 and 3 could be bottom-aligned, but the header would then sit far from its options.
4. The amber accent appears only in the logo mark and the progress dot. That is deliberately quiet; if it is too faint, an amber stub behind the header's code would mark "you are here" more strongly.
5. Keyboard: after going deeper, focus moves to the step heading ("Choose a platform"), so Tab goes to the first option and Shift+Tab reaches Back. Going back puts focus on the card you came from. Escape closes the sheet, then goes up one level.
6. The list is a scroll container in case a level ever has many options. During a transition it switches to overflow: visible so the travelling card isn't clipped. If the player had scrolled that list, the content would snap to the top for that moment. That can't happen with 3 or 4 options, but the native builds should make the header an overlay instead.
7. The prototype has no tokens beyond the reference :root. The only extra values are shadow rgba values on the card paper, which follow the reference's chip and close-button shadow recipe.

built.summary: Each step shows one large title, one small mono prompt ("Choose an area / platform / deck") and at most three calm paper destination cards. A card has a perforated arrow stub and nothing else, except deck cards, which also show the code, card count and a progress track. Areas or platforms with no decks show as a dashed outline that says "No decks yet". A slim flight-path route under the back button gains one waypoint per choice (Start, then Cloud, AWS, CLF), with the amber plane from the game screen marking where you are. Going forward pushes the whole screen left by one width while the route's solid segment draws to the next stop, the plane flies there with the spring, and the new label lands. Going back reverses it. Choosing a deck opens the home-a section sheet, and the deck code becomes the route's final stop.
built.logo: The mark is a small amber boarding-pass stub (46x34, rounded, with semicircle notches on both sides and a dashed ink perforation near the right end) with an ink check mark in the main part, so it reads as a "true" ticket. Next to it is the "Truthy" wordmark in Overpass 800 at 38px, left-aligned. The description under it, in Overpass 600 at 17px, reads: "True or false cards that teach you IT, one swipe at a time." On step 1 the route header is hidden, so the screen shows only the logo, that line, "Choose an area" and the three area cards (Cloud 3 decks, Frontend 1 deck, DevOps "No decks yet").
built.motion:
Forward (step n to n+1), all in one 360ms (--t3) movement:
- Screen push: the outgoing step goes from translateX(0) to translateX(-100%) and opacity 1 to 0.2. The incoming step goes from translateX(100%) to 0. Both use --ease. The two screens stay edge to edge, so they never overlap.
- Route segment: a solid ink bar that grows with transform scaleX(at/3) from its left end, using --ease.
- Plane: rides a full-width layer with translateX(at*100%/3), using --spring, so it settles with a slight overshoot.
- Waypoints: the stop just passed gets an ink dot that scales from 0 to 1 (300ms, --spring, 120ms delay) and replaces its hollow ring. The new stop's mono label fades and rises 5px (220ms, 140ms delay).

Back reverses everything. When a jump skips a step (tapping Start from step 3), the skipped step moves instantly with no transition, so it never sweeps across the screen. Moving from step 1 to 2 also fades the route header in over 220ms. The section sheet is the home-a sheet unchanged (translateY 104% to 0, 420ms --spring, scrim fade). The route sits above the scrim while the sheet is open, so the deck-code stop lands in plain view.

Reduced motion: no transforms, only a sequential opacity fade (outgoing fades out over 120ms, then incoming fades in over 180ms) so the text never overlaps. All route and sheet transitions drop to 1ms.

Only transform and opacity are animated (visibility only flips at the end).

SwiftUI: a NavigationStack-style push using .transition(.asymmetric(insertion: .move(edge: .trailing), removal: .move(edge: .leading).combined(with: .opacity))) inside withAnimation(.timingCurve(0.2,0.7,0.2,1, duration: 0.36)). The route is a persistent overlay. The segment uses .scaleEffect(x: at/3, anchor: .leading), and the plane uses .offset(x:) with .spring(response: 0.36, dampingFraction: 0.7). Each step's title can carry a matchedGeometryEffect id with its route label if a shared element is wanted.

Compose: AnimatedContent(targetState = step) with slideInHorizontally { it } togetherWith slideOutHorizontally { -it } + fadeOut(targetAlpha 0.2), reversed when the step decreases, using tween(360, CubicBezierEasing(0.2f,0.7f,0.2f,1f)). The route uses animateFloatAsState for the scaleX fraction (graphicsLayer with a left transform origin) and a spring for the plane's translationX. Reduced motion uses fadeIn/fadeOut.
built.openQuestions:
1. Route above the scrim: while the sheet is open, the route and back button stay undimmed and tappable. This lets the CLF stop be seen landing and lets the player jump back. The cost is a bright back button over a dimmed screen, and both it and the sheet's X close the sheet. The alternative is to dim the route along with everything else.
2. Start stop: the route begins with a "Start" stop that goes back to the area screen. It is useful, but it is one more label on screen; it could become the small logo mark instead.
3. Empty space below the cards: cards hang from the top under the title for a calm top-down read, which leaves the lower 30 to 40% of the screen empty (more on Next.js, which has one deck). Placing the cards lower would be easier to reach with a thumb but looks less tidy.
4. Data I assumed: RND shows 12% seen, as in home-a. The brief gives progress only for CLF. CDL has no sections, so its sheet shows only "Whole deck". SAA and RND section counts come from home-a.
5. No new tokens. The unavailable cards use translucent paper rgba(253,251,245,.42) with a dashed border in ink at 32% opacity, following the inline ink-rgba values home-a uses.
6. Escape closes the sheet, or steps back one level when the sheet is closed.

built.summary: Each step shows one heading in the same place and two or three large, quiet ticket cards. Step 1 has the Truthy logo and a one-line description above the cards; from step 2 a small pass with Area, Platform and Deck fields takes the logo's place and gets filled in, and a deck opens the home-a section sheet while the pass stays lit above the scrim. On every choice the chosen name travels into its field on the pass while the other options fade and the next ones rise in. Going back runs the same move in reverse.
built.logo: The mark is a small amber ticket with notches on both sides, an ink check (for "true") and a dashed tear line by the stub. It sits next to the "Truthy" wordmark in Overpass 800 at 36px. A 20px ink version of the same mark sits in the pass's amber header, next to the game ticket's wording, so the logo and the pass read as one brand. The description line: "True or false cards that teach you IT, one swipe at a time."
built.motion: Going deeper (1>2, 2>3) is one move of about 360 ms. The heading lifts 10px and fades in 80 ms, and the other cards do the same in 140 ms, ease-out. After a 60 ms hold, a copy of the chosen name flies to its field on the pass in 300 ms using the token --ease (cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.2,1)). It only uses translate and scale: both ends use the same font with line-height 1.2, so scaling 26px to 16px (30px to 16px for the deck code) is the whole morph. The field's blank dashes fade out at 120 to 220 ms, and the field shows its value once the name lands. The next heading and cards rise from translateY(24px) with opacity 0 to 1, starting at 110 ms with 25 ms between items over 240 ms. Between steps 1 and 2 the top area also swaps: the logo lifts 12px and fades in 160 ms, and the back button and pass rise 12px into the same place starting at 100 ms. Back reverses everything: the value flies from the pass to the card it came from, the current cards sink 10px and fade, the previous ones drop in from -24px, and the dashes come back. Choosing a deck flies its code into the Deck field while home-a's sheet rises with --spring in 420 ms. The pass sits above the scrim (z-index), so the finished pass stays lit; closing the sheet flies the code back to its card. Reduced motion: nothing moves; the old step fades out in 100 ms and the new one fades in from 90 to 230 ms, so text never overlaps. Only transform and opacity are used. In SwiftUI the name is a matchedGeometryEffect between the card label and the pass field (one Namespace per field), and the steps are a transition of .opacity combined with .offset(y: ±24). In Compose it is SharedTransitionLayout with Modifier.sharedElement(key = field) inside AnimatedContent on the step, using fadeIn + slideInVertically for entering and fadeOut + slideOutVertically for leaving. Both can use spring(dampingRatio ~0.8) or tween(360, the matching cubic easing), and the reverse direction comes from AnimatedContent's targetState comparison or SwiftUI's navigation direction.

review.comparison:
All three now meet the basic shape the client asked for: logo, one line and three big area cards; an animated move to AWS / Google Cloud / Azure; an animated move to CLF / SAA; and the earlier section sheet reused. All three use the same :root, Overpass type and sky paper as game-classic.html. The difference is how much each one puts around the cards.

Recommendation: A. It is the strictest answer to 'too complicated'. Each step is a header plus a few cards and nothing else. One card form is used at every level, and the motion explains the hierarchy instead of decorating it: the card you tap becomes 'where you are', and Back plays it in reverse. With 8 areas its list already scrolled under a fixed header, and it was the only one of the three that did before my fixes. Before showing it to the client, fix one thing: the header card looks tappable but is not.

B comes second. The route header is the best 'where am I and how do I go back' device of the three, since it shows the full path and every past stop is tappable. The horizontal push is the most familiar mobile motion. But it states the location three times and makes the question the smallest text, and it could not scroll and took accidental double taps until I fixed both.

C is the most on-metaphor and links best into the game's boarding pass. It is also the heaviest: an amber pass bar and three fields above every decision, which is exactly the busy feel the client rejected.

Scale: with 8 areas, all three show about 3.5 area cards under the logo and scroll the rest. With 10 decks on one platform, all three scroll inside a fixed header. A and B keep about 5 to 6 decks in view; C keeps about 4 because of its taller top zone.

What I checked: shot2 gave 'ok (4 shots)' for each variant, and I read every PNG. My Playwright driver ran with channel chrome at 390x844 (scratchpad/tools/drive-browse.mjs, with --big and --reduce). It found no broken paths, dead controls, leftover half-faded elements or overflow after the fixes. Frames frozen at 120 and 250 ms are in scratchpad/review/{a,b,c}-motion.png.

Two notes: the old browse-a-focus.png and browse-a-mid-*.png in shots/ were left by an earlier pass and still show the removed CLD codes; I left them alone because I was told not to touch other files. I edited only browse-a.html, browse-b.html and browse-c.html, and wrote only the 12 fresh PNGs in shots/.
